messages:
alex (support): FYI escalation from AcmeCorp — they're seeing a bunch of 429s around 11:58-12:10 PST during their nightly batch sync. They say they didn't change anything. Sample from their client: `x-rate-limit-remaining: 0`, `x-request-id: req_8a3f9`.

ryan (sre): Can you paste one of our internal log lines for that request_id and the header block? Need to know route/model and whether it hit the global or per-customer quota.

alex (support): Pasting sanitized log snippet below. This is from prod-logs (filtered by request_id).
```json
{"ts":"2026-03-14T19:58:03Z","request_id":"req_8a3f9","client_id":"acct_acme_123","route":"/v1/generate","model":"redwood/gpt-3.1-medium","status":429,"headers":{"x-rate-limit-remaining":"0","x-rate-limit-reset":"2026-03-14T19:59:00Z"},"quota_policy":"per_minute_burst=100, sustained=10/min"}
```
Quick jq to pull other lines: `pgrep -f log-forwarder && jq 'select(.client_id==\"acct_acme_123\")' prod-logs-2026-03-14.log | less`

sara (product): That model is served out of the small-hosted pool with fairly tight concurrency. If their burst was user-driven (many parallel requests), they can hit burst buckets fast. Do we know if they were on Hosted or Dedicated?

alex (support): Customer says "hosted". They are on Growth plan (per-minute quotas).

dan (support): Steps to attribute quickly:
1) Prometheus query for the window: 
```
sum by (customer_id, route, model) (increase(redwood_api_responses_total{code="429"}[15m]))
```
This will show if 429s are concentrated on a single route/model or customer.
2) Burn rate:
```
sum by (customer_id) (increase(redwood_tokens_consumed_total[10m]))
```
3) Cross-reference `client_id` -> plan & burst limits from the customers DB: 
```
SELECT id, plan, burst_limit_per_minute FROM customers WHERE id='acct_acme_123';
```

ops-bot: :rotating_light: rate-limit-alert fired for prod-cluster-1 (rule: per_customer_429_rate) — https://observability.internal/alerts/2321

ryan (sre): Nice. Dashboards we should check/add ASAP:
- Heatmap: 429s by minute x route (to see whether a single endpoint is noisy)
- Top offending customers by 429 count (last 1h, 6h)
- Token burn vs quota remaining per customer (rolling 5m window)
- Model-level concurrency vs allowed concurrency (to spot hot-model throttles)

Suggested alerting tweaks:
- Alert when `increase(redwood_api_responses_total{code="429",customer_id!="internal"}[5m]) > 50` for any customer and sustained for 3m.
- Alert when `sum by (route) (increase(redwood_api_responses_total{code="429"}[5m]))` shows a single route > 30 for 1m (possible misbehaving integration).

alex (support): Customer is asking how we decide whether throttling is per-customer or global. Short answer?

ryan (sre): We have layered quotas: token-based per-customer (burst + sustained), per-route safeguards, and global cluster-level protective limits. The headers they get are the most direct clue: `x-rate-limit-remaining` reflects their customer-bucket. If header shows 0 and `x-rate-limit-policy` includes per_customer settings, it's their quota. If headers are missing but we return 429, it might be a global protect firing.

sara (product): For attribution, also check request trace: `x-request-id` -> distributed trace in Tempo/jaeger. If traces show a shared upstream queue/backpressure spike across many customers, that's a cluster event. If concentrated to one customer, it's quota.

dan (support): Repro steps for the customer (do in staging):
- Use this script to simulate their burst (runs 200 parallel requests over 30s):
```bash
# staging only
wrk -t10 -c200 -d30s -H "Authorization: Bearer <their-staging-token>" "https://staging.api.redwood.com/v1/generate"
```
- Watch headers: `curl -I` on a handful of requests to inspect `x-rate-limit-*`.
- Note any 429s and collect request_ids.

ryan (sre): Important safety note: do not run that in prod without coordination — it will affect other customers. Use a staging token mapped to the same plan if possible.

alex (support): Customer sent a screenshot of headers and a few request_ids. I'm going to run the PromQL queries and paste results here.

(5 minutes later)
alex (support): PromQL results: `increase(...429...)[15m]` shows 312 429s for acct_acme_123 between 19:55 and 20:10. Top route is `/v1/generate`. Token burn spike matches the batch window.

ryan (sre): OK that points to per-customer quota exhaustion. Short-term mitigations:
- Increase their burst quota temporarily (admin console)
- Recommend throttling/backoff on their client side (exponential backoff with jitter)
- If they need sustained higher throughput, propose Dedicated or bumped plan.

sara (product): To make this easier next time, action items:
- Add a dashboard tile on support console showing current `x-rate-limit-remaining` per active customer (top 25)
- Add a support playbook link in the alert that includes the exact PromQL and SQL snippets above

dan (support): Admin command to bump burst (internal API, example):
```
curl -X POST "https://console.internal.redwood/api/admin/customers/acct_acme_123/quotas" -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"burst_limit_per_minute":200, "note":"temp bump for batch window 2026-03-14"}'
```
Do we want to do a one-off bump now?

alex (support): Customer asked for a short bump — I'll request a +100 burst for 24h and monitor.

ryan (sre): I'll add a temporary dashboard panel and create the alert with the thresholds above. Also instrument an additional label in logs `customer_burst_exhausted=true` when we return 429 for a quota. That will make attribution trivial in the future.

sara (product): Assigning follow-ups: ryan for dashboard & instrumentation, alex to own customer comms and temp bump, dan to add playbook doc. :thumbsup:

ops-bot: Created ticket RNW-4213 assigned to ryan (sre).

alex (support): Thanks all — I'll confirm with customer once the bump is applied and share guidance for client-side backoff.

ryan (sre): Also note: add a trace-based synthetic that hits `/v1/generate` once a minute per plan to detect early burn spikes. Will reduce noisy escalations.

sara (product): Great — let's follow up in #product-next-week with measured impact after 24h.

dan (support): I'll draft the public support KB on "Why am I getting 429s — how to decode headers and attribute" and include the playbook.

alex (support): Closing loop, example customer message I sent: "We believe this was your plan-level burst bucket being consumed by parallel batch workers. We've temporarily increased your burst limit by 100 for 24 hours while you implement client-side backoff; if you expect sustained higher throughput we can discuss upgrading to Dedicated capacity." Customer responded :thumbsup: and will test tonight.
